# Introduction

Bengaluru is the one Indian city where the OAQ platform carries two independent
PM2.5 monitoring networks at once. One is CPCB, the government reference network
of regulatory-grade Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations. The
other is Airnet, a dense network of low-cost sensors run by CSTEP.

This vignette puts them head to head over the same months (March–April 2026) in
the same city. Do the low-cost Airnet sensors reproduce the signal the CPCB
reference network measures? A sensor network can get the daily trend right and
still report the wrong level, so we look at trend, level, and spatial coverage
separately.

The reason it matters: if dense low-cost sensors hold up, they can extend
reference monitoring into the gaps a sparse official network leaves behind.

---

# Data sources

Both networks are read from the OAQ platform via the same functions, differing
only in the `provider` argument. Both return daily means per station.

| Network | `provider` | Role | Pollutants | Density |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPCB | `"cpcb"` | Regulatory reference | PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NOx, met | Sparse |
| Airnet (CSTEP) | `"airnet"` | Low-cost sensors | PM2.5, PM10 | Dense |

---

# Setup

```{r packages}
library(vayuayan)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(ggrepel)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
library(here)
```

```{r paths}
vignettes_dir <- here::here("vignettes")
fig_dir <- file.path(vignettes_dir, "figures/blr_networks")
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

---

# Fetch both networks

```{r oaq-session}
session <- oaq_session()
```

`oaq_fetch_monthly_stations()` pulls every station for each provider in a city
across the chosen months and returns one tidy table of daily readings, already
joined to station coordinates.

```{r fetch-data, cache=TRUE}
both <- oaq_fetch_monthly_stations(
  session, c("cpcb", "airnet"),
  year = 2026, months = c("03", "04"), city = "Bengaluru"
) |>
  mutate(network = recode(provider,
    cpcb   = "CPCB reference",
    airnet = "Airnet low-cost"
  ))

both |>
  filter(!is.na(pm25)) |>
  group_by(network) |>
  summarise(
    stations     = n_distinct(station_id),
    station_days = n(),
    median_pm25  = round(median(pm25), 1),
    iqr_low      = round(quantile(pm25, 0.25), 1),
    iqr_high     = round(quantile(pm25, 0.75), 1),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Bengaluru PM2.5 coverage, March–April 2026")
```

Network colours used throughout:

```{r colours}
net_colors <- c(
  "CPCB reference"  = "#d73027",
  "Airnet low-cost" = "#4575b4"
)
```

---

# Daily city trend

For each network we take the cross-station median per day (the city signal) and
the inter-quartile range (the spread between sensors). If the low-cost network
reproduces the reference signal, the two median lines should track together.

```{r daily-summary}
daily <- both |>
  filter(!is.na(pm25)) |>
  group_by(network, date) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(pm25),
    p25 = quantile(pm25, 0.25),
    p75 = quantile(pm25, 0.75),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r daily-plot, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Daily city-median PM2.5 in Bengaluru, March–April 2026. Lines = cross-station median per network; ribbons = inter-quartile range. The two networks follow the same day-to-day trend, but Airnet (blue) sits consistently below the CPCB reference (red), with the gap largest on high-pollution days."}
ggplot(daily, aes(x = date, colour = network, fill = network)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p25, ymax = p75), alpha = 0.18, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 15, linetype = "dotted", colour = "orange", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text",
    x = min(daily$date), y = 17,
    label = "WHO 24hr (15 µg/m³)", size = 3, colour = "tan4", hjust = 0
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%d %b", date_breaks = "1 week") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "Bengaluru daily PM2.5: CPCB reference vs Airnet low-cost (2026)",
    subtitle = "Line = cross-station median | ribbon = inter-quartile range",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = expression(paste("PM2.5 (", mu, "g/m"^3, ")")),
    caption  = "Source: OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in) — providers cpcb + airnet"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, colour = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig1_daily_trend.png"), width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Day-matched agreement

Aligning the two networks by day, we plot the Airnet city median against the
CPCB city median for the same date. Points on the 1:1 line mean the low-cost
network reproduces the reference reading. A fit line below 1:1 means Airnet reads
low, and a slope under 1 means it under-responds as pollution rises.

```{r day-matched}
matched <- daily |>
  select(network, date, median) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = network, values_from = median) |>
  rename(cpcb = `CPCB reference`, airnet = `Airnet low-cost`) |>
  filter(!is.na(cpcb), !is.na(airnet))

fit <- lm(airnet ~ cpcb, data = matched)
r_val <- cor(matched$cpcb, matched$airnet)
bias <- mean(matched$airnet - matched$cpcb)

cat("Matched days:", nrow(matched), "\n")
cat("Pearson r:", round(r_val, 3), "\n")
cat("Mean bias (Airnet − CPCB):", round(bias, 1), "µg/m³\n")
cat("Slope:", round(coef(fit)[2], 2), "\n")
```

```{r day-matched-plot, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=6, fig.cap="Airnet vs CPCB city-median PM2.5, day-matched (March–April 2026). Each point is one day. Dashed line = 1:1; red line = linear fit."}
ggplot(matched, aes(x = cpcb, y = airnet)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(colour = "#4575b4", size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "firebrick", fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2) +
  annotate("text",
    x = min(matched$cpcb), y = max(matched$airnet),
    label = sprintf(
      "r = %.2f\nbias = %+.1f µg/m³\nslope = %.2f",
      r_val, bias, coef(fit)[2]
    ),
    hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4, colour = "grey20"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³")) +
  labs(
    title = "Day-matched agreement: Airnet vs CPCB",
    x = expression(paste("CPCB city median PM"[2.5])),
    y = expression(paste("Airnet city median PM"[2.5])),
    caption = "Source: OAQ platform | Bengaluru | March–April 2026"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig2_day_matched.png"), width = 6, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Spatial coverage

The two networks differ most in density. The map shows every station, sized by
its mean PM2.5 over the period, over Bengaluru's ward boundaries.

```{r blr-boundary}
blr_boundary <- sf::st_read(
  "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/bengaluru.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) |> sf::st_transform(4326)
```

```{r station-means}
station_means <- both |>
  filter(!is.na(pm25), !is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) |>
  group_by(network, station_id, lat, lon) |>
  summarise(mean_pm25 = mean(pm25), n_days = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_days >= 10)

station_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(station_means, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
```

```{r station-map, fig.height=7, fig.width=9, fig.cap="Monitoring network density in Bengaluru. Red = CPCB reference stations, blue = Airnet low-cost sensors. Point size = mean PM2.5 (March–April 2026). The low-cost network is roughly 4x denser."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = blr_boundary, fill = "grey97", colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(
    data = station_sf,
    aes(colour = network, size = mean_pm25),
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 6), name = expression(paste("Mean PM"[2.5]))) +
  labs(
    title = "Bengaluru monitoring networks: reference vs low-cost",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "CPCB: %d stations | Airnet: %d stations (≥10 valid days)",
      sum(station_means$network == "CPCB reference"),
      sum(station_means$network == "Airnet low-cost")
    ),
    caption = "Source: OAQ platform + BharatViz ward boundaries"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid      = element_blank(),
    axis.text       = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig3_network_map.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Controlling for location

The city-median comparison has a confound: the two networks do not cover the
same ground. CPCB stations cluster in central Bengaluru, while Airnet reaches
the periphery. If the outskirts are genuinely cleaner, Airnet would read lower
even with a perfect sensor, and the bias above would be a sampling artefact
rather than a sensor effect.

To separate the two, we pair each Airnet sensor with its nearest CPCB station
and keep only pairs within a short distance, so each comparison is effectively
same-location. If the low bias survives this control, it comes from the sensors,
not the geography.

```{r distance-control}
cpcb_st <- station_means |> filter(network == "CPCB reference")
air_st <- station_means |> filter(network == "Airnet low-cost")

paired <- nearest_stations(
  air_st, cpcb_st,
  k = 1, from_id = "station_id", to_id = "station_id"
) |>
  left_join(
    air_st |> select(station_id, airnet_pm25 = mean_pm25),
    by = c("from_id" = "station_id")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    cpcb_st |> select(station_id, cpcb_pm25 = mean_pm25),
    by = c("to_id" = "station_id")
  )

control_table <- paired |>
  crossing(radius = c(3, 5, 8)) |>
  filter(dist_km <= radius) |>
  group_by(radius) |>
  summarise(
    `Co-located pairs` = n(),
    `Mean Airnet`      = round(mean(airnet_pm25), 1),
    `Mean CPCB`        = round(mean(cpcb_pm25), 1),
    `Mean difference`  = round(mean(airnet_pm25 - cpcb_pm25), 1)
  ) |>
  mutate(`Max pairing distance` = paste0("≤ ", radius, " km"), .before = 1) |>
  select(-radius)

uncontrolled_diff <- round(median(air_st$mean_pm25) - median(cpcb_st$mean_pm25), 1)

knitr::kable(control_table,
  caption = sprintf(
    "Airnet minus CPCB after distance pairing. Uncontrolled city-median difference: %s µg/m³.",
    uncontrolled_diff
  )
)
```

The median Airnet sensor sits about 3 km from a CPCB station, so the pairing is
tight. The low bias hardly moves when we restrict to co-located pairs, which
means it is a property of the sensors rather than of where they happen to sit.

---

# Distribution comparison

The daily median hides the shape of the readings. Plotting the full
distribution of station-days for each network shows where they overlap and
where they part. A tighter low-cost distribution can mean genuinely lower
variability or sensor smoothing.

```{r distribution-plot, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Distribution of daily station PM2.5 readings by network, March–April 2026. Each observation is one station on one day."}
obs <- both |> filter(!is.na(pm25))

ggplot(obs, aes(x = pm25, fill = network, colour = network)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(
    data = obs |> group_by(network) |> summarise(m = median(pm25), .groups = "drop"),
    aes(xintercept = m, colour = network), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " µg/m³"), limits = c(0, 150)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = net_colors, name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title    = "PM2.5 reading distribution: CPCB vs Airnet",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines = network medians",
    x        = expression(paste("Daily station PM"[2.5])),
    y        = "Density",
    caption  = "Source: OAQ platform | Bengaluru | March–April 2026"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig4_distribution.png"), width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Conclusion

```{r conclusion-stats, echo=FALSE}
cpcb_med <- round(median(both$pm25[both$provider == "cpcb"], na.rm = TRUE), 1)
airnet_med <- round(median(both$pm25[both$provider == "airnet"], na.rm = TRUE), 1)
r_round <- round(r_val, 2)
bias_round <- round(bias, 1)
slope_round <- round(coef(fit)[2], 2)
n_cpcb <- sum(station_means$network == "CPCB reference")
n_airnet <- sum(station_means$network == "Airnet low-cost")
```

Over March–April 2026 in Bengaluru, the Airnet low-cost network gets the timing
right and the magnitude wrong.

On timing, the agreement is strong. The two city-median lines rise and fall on
the same days, with a day-matched correlation of `r r_round`, so a low-cost
network reliably captures when Bengaluru's air gets worse. On magnitude, Airnet
reads low. Its network-median PM2.5 is `r airnet_med` µg/m³ against
`r cpcb_med` µg/m³ for CPCB, a mean bias of `r bias_round` µg/m³, and the
regression slope of `r slope_round` shows the gap widening as concentrations
climb. The two networks agree on clean days, but Airnet increasingly under-reads
the pollution peaks that CPCB records. The cause is the sensors, not the
geography: pairing each Airnet sensor with a CPCB station within a few
kilometres leaves the low bias almost unchanged. Range compression like this is
a familiar low-cost-sensor trait, and it is the main reason raw Airnet values
should not be read as absolute levels.

Where the low-cost network clearly wins is coverage. Airnet contributes
`r n_airnet` usable stations to CPCB's `r n_cpcb`, reaching the city's periphery
where the reference network has no monitors at all.

So the two are complementary rather than interchangeable. Airnet is reliable for
trend and for filling spatial gaps, but its readings need calibration against
the CPCB reference before they stand in as absolute concentrations, especially
during high-pollution episodes. And the reference network is still the only
source for NO2, SO2, CO, and O3, which Airnet does not measure at all.
